Container.Name: IT-Vault
Container.Description: IT-Vault is a self-hosted IT asset register and helpdesk: assets, employees, contracts, tickets, a public request portal, LDAP/AD sync, network scanning, QR labels and e-signed handovers. Bring your own MariaDB or MySQL.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: The port you will open IT-Vault on.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Session key and the saved database pointer. Keep this: losing it signs everyone out and forgets which database to use.

Config.Name: Invoices
Config.Description: Invoices and proof-of-purchase files attached to assets.

Config.Name: Backups
Config.Description: Where scheduled backups are written. Put this on a share you actually back up.

Config.Name: Database host
Config.Description: Your MariaDB/MySQL server. For a MariaDB container on this Unraid box, use the server's LAN IP (bridge networking cannot reach it by container name). Leave empty to be asked by the setup wizard instead.

Config.Name: Database name
Config.Description: The empty database you created for IT-Vault.

Config.Name: Database user
Config.Description: A user with rights on that database -- not root.

Config.Name: Public URL
Config.Description: The address people reach this on from outside, e.g. https://itvault.example.com. Used for the links in acknowledgement and portal emails, which are useless if they point at a LAN address. Leave empty if you only use it on the LAN.

Config.Name: Force secure cookies
Config.Description: Set to 1 to insist the session cookie is only ever sent over HTTPS. Leave empty and it is decided per request, which is right if you reach it both ways.

Config.Name: Session secret
Config.Description: Leave empty. IT-Vault generates a strong one on first start and keeps it in the data path above, which beats any value typed into a template -- a known secret lets anyone forge an admin session. Set it only to share one key across several instances.
